text:
maria: Quick follow-up to the RFC I posted yesterday about the enrichment-lane extract. I sketched a safety-first cutover plan and wanted quick eyes before I file the PR. TL;DR: incremental extract of the enricher into a new service with a transparent proxy, canary progression, and a rewind-capable test harness.

alex: Sounds reasonable. call out ownership clearly so we avoid dual-write ambiguity during the rollover.

maria: Ownership stays with the existing writer until final flip. steps: 1) read-through proxy that forwards to original writer, 2) shadow writes to new service (non-authoritative), 3) canary reads from new service for sampled tenants, 4) flip authoritative after validation.

sam: For the shadow phase how are we validating parity? full diffs or sampled checks?

maria: Deterministic sample sets + lightweight diff checker. well also have a golden prompt set to exercise edge behaviors. diffs > threshold => automatic halt.

jordan: Operational: the proxy adds an extra hop. can we exempt hotpath tenants so they don't see latency regression?

maria: Yes, we have tenant-affinity config. critical tenants stay on direct path until they pass validation. example routing snippet included in the playbook.

alex: Rollback plan? need fast failover if new service misbehaves at scale.

maria: Canary progression (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%), each step gated by automated SLO checks (p95, error-rate, diff-rate). failing checks trigger immediate traffic drain and route hump back to direct.

infra-bot: deploy-check: canary pipeline exists for branch `enricher/extract-v3`  - no blockers found. :white_check_mark:

sam: Cache & KV consistency are tricky. New service will present a read-through cache; we need a harness that simulates cold and warm KV states and verifies staleness windows.

maria: Ill add a KV warmup job to the canary runbook and a `migrate-metadata` flag to mark ownership after validation.

jordan: Security & compliance: ensure audit logs clearly show which service authored the final writes during transition. customers will ask for an attestation trail.

maria: Called that out in the RFC appendix: audit field, tenant-scoped writer id, and KMS key usage for migrated items.

alex: We should codify roll-forward vs roll-back thresholds. I can help tune a short spreadsheet for p95, diff %, and error-rate limits.

maria: Please do. Quick asks: @alex review ownership wording? @sam outline KV warmup test plan? @jordan sanity-check latency escape hatch?

alex: Will review today.

sam: I'll prototype a minimal KV warmup tool and share commands. proto usage: `./kv-warmup --tenants sample-list.txt --parallel 32 --verify-diff`

jordan: Latency escape hatch looks fine; we can stage critical tenants in micro-batches if needed.

maria: Thanks. If no objections Ill open the PR with the safety playbook and staged rollout script tomorrow morning. :rocket:

alex: +1

sam: +1

jordan: +1

maria: Posted the RFC and appendix here: https://redwood.example.com/rfcs/enricher-extract -- feedback welcome.
